core_intuitions: The whole chapter is ONE loop that wires five already-built components (data, model, optimizer+schedule, tokenizer, config) into train.py; nothing here is a new component, only the orchestration that spends the GPU-hours.

Effective batch = micro_batch x seq_len x grad_accum_steps: you reach a 524k-token optimizer step by ACCUMULATING gradients over N micro-batches - zero grads ONCE per step (not per micro-batch), scale each micro-loss by 1/N before backward so the summed gradient equals the true batch-mean gradient.

The per-step cadence is fixed: set LR (WSD) -> N forward/backward accumulations -> ONE global grad-norm clip across ALL params -> optimizer.step(); the clip is joint over Muon-bound and AdamW-bound params so one group's blow-up can't hide behind the other's normal gradients.

GPU-Util (nvidia-smi) only says a kernel was running; MFU = 6*N*(tokens/s) / peak_FLOPs says what fraction of the hardware's matmul throughput you actually bought - util can read ~100% while MFU sits far below, and MFU is what maps to GPU-hours and dollars.

At 100M params ACTIVATIONS dominate training memory, not weights/optimizer state; the residual-stream term scales with n_layers (30x), so activation checkpointing collapses that 30x to a single block's worth of live activations - trading ~30% recompute FLOPs for a large memory cut that lets 24GB/16GB tiers fit.

A checkpoint must capture EVERYTHING that determines the future - model + optimizer state + step counter + data-loader cursor + all RNG states - written atomically (tmp file + rename); miss any one (especially the data cursor or Muon momentum) and 'resume' silently diverges from an uninterrupted run.

One recipe, three tiers: the same train.py trains on A100/4090/T4 - only micro_batch, grad_accum, activation checkpointing, and precision (bf16 vs fp16+GradScaler) move, all preserving the SAME 524k-token effective batch.

new_figures.name: grad-accum-effective-batch
new_figures.concept: How grad_accum_steps micro-batches accumulate into one 524k-token optimizer step: zero once, run N forward/backward passes each scaled by 1/N, gradients add up in the same buffer, then a single clip + step - equal to one giant batch.
new_figures.rationale: This is the chapter's central, most error-prone mechanic (the prose gives it a whole warning box about the zero-inside-the-loop bug). Readers can recite 'micro x accum = effective batch' but often don't SEE why the gradient buffer accumulates, why loss is divided by N before backward, or why zeroing per micro-batch secretly runs 8 tiny steps. A figure that shows the buffer filling across N passes and discharging in one step makes the mean-gradient equivalence and the pitfall click at once.
new_figures.placement: Gradient accumulation: micro-batch x accum = effective batch
new_figures.brief: A process figure with a strong static frame: the accumulate-then-step cadence of ONE optimizer step. Use small illustrative integers (N = grad_accum_steps = 4 is enough to read cleanly; annotate 'here N=8, 32x2048 tokens each = 524,288-token effective batch'). LAYOUT left-to-right: a row of N micro-batch tiles (each labeled 'micro-batch i: 32 x 2048 tokens') feeding a shared central 'gradient buffer' (draw as an accumulator tank / stacked bar). Above each micro-batch show its mini-pipeline: 'forward (bf16 autocast) -> loss/N -> backward'. Each backward ADDS its contribution into the same buffer (show the buffer level rising by roughly equal increments across the N passes, and label 'grads SUM across passes - buffer is NOT zeroed between them'). At the top-left, a single 'optimizer.zero_grad() - ONCE per step' marker with an arrow showing it fires only before micro-batch 1. On the right, after the buffer is full, a single discharge path: 'clip_grad_norm_ (global, c=1.0) -> optimizer.step() -> zero for next step'. Add a compact equivalence callout: 'sum of (grad of loss_i / N) == grad of mean loss over all 524,288 tokens == what one giant batch would give'. Include a small red-flagged PITFALL inset (clearly separated, not the main path): 'zero_grad() inside the loop => N independent 65k-token steps at 1/8 the intended batch - loss still falls, so easy to miss'. ANIMATION (enhancement only; static frame must fully convey it): sweep through micro-batches 1..N one at a time, the current tile highlights, its forward->backward runs, the buffer level steps up; after the Nth, the buffer flashes and discharges through clip -> step -> reset to empty, then loop. Theme-safe: theme ink for text/axes, one accent for the micro-batch/forward path, a second accent for the accumulating gradient buffer, and a distinct warning accent used ONLY for the pitfall inset. No hardcoded primary colors, everything inside the viewBox, clear reading order, no overlapping labels; the buffer increments and the 'zero once / step once' markers must be legible in both light and dark.

new_figures.name: mfu-vs-gpu-util
new_figures.concept: Why nvidia-smi's GPU-Util misleads and MFU is the metric that matters: util reads ~100% whenever ANY kernel runs, while MFU = achieved FLOPs/s (6*N*tokens/s) divided by peak FLOPs/s measures the fraction of the hardware's matmul throughput you actually paid for.
new_figures.rationale: The measurement section's entire point - and the Interview Corner Q&A - hinges on the gap between 'busy' and 'productive'. This distinction is abstract in prose but instantly visual: a nearly-full util bar next to a half-full MFU bar, with the empty region labeled as idle tensor cores / wasted GPU-hours, converts the 6ND formula and the '85% util, 18% MFU' scenario into one picture that also directly maps to dollars.
new_figures.placement: Measuring Throughput and Model FLOPs Utilization
new_figures.brief: A single static infographic contrasting two vertical bars against the SAME 'peak' ceiling, both scaled 0..100% of the accelerator. LEFT BAR 'GPU-Util (nvidia-smi)': filled to ~high (label '~100% - a kernel was running during the sampling window'); annotate that it's a binary busy/idle sampler - 'says NOTHING about whether that kernel was a peak matmul or a tiny memory-bound op'. RIGHT BAR 'MFU = achieved / peak FLOPs': filled only partway (use an illustrative fraction consistent with the chapter, e.g. ~45% for a well-tuned loop; do NOT invent a benchmark - label it as illustrative). The UNFILLED top portion of the MFU bar is the key visual: hatch/shade it and label 'idle tensor cores = GPU-hours you paid for but didn't use'. Between the bars, place the defining formula prominently: 'MFU = 6 * N * (tokens/s) / peak_FLOPs' with a one-line gloss '6 FLOPs / parameter / token (forward+backward, the 6ND rule)'. Along the bottom, a small 'so what' strip translating MFU to money: 'higher MFU -> same model in fewer GPU-hours -> lower cost' (schematic, no dollar figures unless using the chapter's own ~USD 40-100 envelope as illustrative). Optionally include a faint second MFU bar for the pathological interview case ('85% util but 18% MFU - unfused/small-op-bound') to underline that util and MFU can diverge wildly - keep it clearly labeled illustrative. Theme-safe: theme ink for text and the peak ceiling line, one accent for the achieved/filled region, a muted hatch for the wasted region; both bars, the ceiling, the formula, and the wasted-region label must read with equal strength in light and dark. Everything inside the viewBox, no overlapping labels, clear left(util)-to-right(MFU) reading order.

new_figures.name: training-memory-budget
new_figures.concept: Where the GPU's memory actually goes during training and what activation checkpointing changes: weights/grads/optimizer state are small fixed terms, activations dominate and scale with n_layers, and checkpointing collapses the 30x residual-stream term to one block's worth.
new_figures.rationale: The memory worked example, the checkpointing lever, and the whole three-tier table all rest on one fact readers rarely internalize - at 100M params activations, not weights, dominate, and the dominant term is multiplied by n_layers. A stacked-budget figure that shows the tall activation column shrinking when checkpointing is turned on is exactly what makes the A100-fits / 4090-needs-checkpointing decision (and the tier table) obvious, and it grounds the memory/compute trade-off referenced from the efficiency chapters.
new_figures.brief: A static side-by-side stacked-bar comparison of the training memory footprint for ONE micro-batch, 'checkpointing OFF' vs 'checkpointing ON', against a labeled VRAM ceiling. Use the chapter's own on-the-order-of magnitudes (label them illustrative, not exact): fp32 master weights ~0.4 GB, gradients ~0.4 GB (bf16), optimizer state ~0.9 GB (Muon momentum + AdamW m/v), and ACTIVATIONS ~10-15 GB - the visibly dominant block. LEFT BAR (OFF): stack the small fixed terms (weights, grads, optimizer state) as thin segments at the bottom, then a TALL activations segment on top, itself visually broken into 'residual stream saved at each of 30 blocks (~2 GB)' + 'SwiGLU intermediate x 30 blocks (~5.5 GB)' + 'attention/QK-norm/MLP up-gate (a few GB)'. Annotate the activation block 'scales with n_layers = 30 - this is the term that dominates'. RIGHT BAR (ON): identical small fixed terms, but the activations block collapses dramatically - label 'checkpointing stores only block BOUNDARIES and recomputes each block in backward: 30x residual term -> ~1 block live'; show a much shorter activations segment, and add a small side-cost tag '+~30% FLOPs (one extra forward per checkpointed block)'. Draw TWO horizontal ceiling lines across both bars: 'A100 80 GB' (far above both) and 'RTX 4090 24 GB' (between the OFF and ON activation heights) so the reader literally SEES that the OFF bar overshoots 24 GB while the ON bar fits - directly explaining why the 4090 tier turns checkpointing on and drops micro-batch from 32 to 8. Keep all numbers tagged 'illustrative, on the order of'. Theme-safe: theme ink for axes/ceilings/labels, distinct muted accents for the fixed terms and one prominent accent for the activations block (same color across both bars so the shrink is obvious); ceiling lines and their labels legible in both themes. Everything inside the viewBox, no overlapping labels, clear OFF(left)->ON(right) reading order; a single static frame fully conveys it - no animation.

summary: A concept-rich, entirely figure-free capstone chapter whose serviceable ASCII data-flow diagram already covers the high-level orchestration, so the payoff is in the three mechanisms readers most often get wrong or hand-wave. Priority-1 figures: (1) grad-accum-effective-batch - an animated-with-strong-static view of the accumulate-then-step cadence, the 1/N loss scaling, and the zero-once pitfall (the chapter's central mechanic and its warning box); (2) mfu-vs-gpu-util - a static two-bar contrast making the 'busy vs productive' gap and the 6N*tok/s / peak formula concrete, directly serving the measurement section and Interview Corner. Priority-2: (3) training-memory-budget - a static OFF-vs-ON stacked-bar showing activations dominate and scale with n_layers, with A100/4090 ceiling lines that explain the tier table and the checkpointing decision. No existing figures to audit; checkpoint-anatomy and the scale-out DDP/FSDP material are adequately served by prose and code and do not warrant figures at this altitude.
